minutes.headline: Commission approved the amended permit for the 380-400 Electric Ave building and added a 5% technology fee.
minutes.summary: Several hearings were continued to March 6, including the 5 Electric Ave addition, the 190 Electric Ave solar project, 400 Electric Ave and the Bell retaining wall. The commission approved the amended notice of intent for the 380/390/400 Electric Ave project with an erosion-control condition. It also heard a land acquisition pitch for the Saliba land, voted to add a technology fee for online filings, and spent a long stretch revising the Lake Shirley order of conditions.

public_comment.topic: A resident spoke in support of the 190 Electric Avenue solar project and urged heavy replanting to restore the previously logged land.

budget_items.what_was_said: The commission agreed to add a flat technology surcharge on all permit fees for online applications. It would be a separate line so it can be adjusted without changing every fee.
A first batch of tickets for a violation was issued, and the fines go into the general fund, not a revolving account.
A speaker mentioned a rough value for the Saliba land, and appraisals, grants and Town Meeting matching funds were discussed.

decisions.decision: The 5 Electric Ave applicant will submit an updated plan moving the dumpster pad to the parking lot corner, relocating the cooler out of the 30-foot no-disturbance zone, and showing all equipment.
The solar applicant will submit a revised plan with seed mix, treeline adjustments, a schedule and replication details, and the commission awaits a DEP number and the peer review report.
Lake Shirley order-of-conditions edits will be sent to Matt, with a 14-day pretreatment report deadline, five clarity locations and written notice to the town manager.
The commission will follow up on the Saliba land with open space contacts, with appraisals and Town Meeting funding as next steps.

what_happened.line: A motion to approve the amended notice of intent for 380/390/400 Electric Ave, with erosion protection kept until the gas station is complete, was made; the outcome is not audible.
A motion to add a flat technology surcharge to wetland permit fees for online applications was made; the outcome is not audible in the recording.
Hearings on the 5 Electric Ave addition, the 190 Electric Ave solar project, the Bell retaining wall and 400 Electric Ave were each continued to March 6.
Review of the Lake Shirley order of conditions ended without resolution; edits will be sent out, with a pretreatment report deadline and written notice to the town manager.
The commission heard a proposal to acquire the Saliba land and will follow up with open space contacts, with appraisals and Town Meeting funding as next steps.

why_it_matters: The Electric Ave approval and the continued hearings shape what gets built near wetlands on that corridor, and the recording does not make clear that the approval passed.

A technology surcharge would add a separate line to permit costs for anyone filing online, and the Saliba land purchase would likely need Town Meeting funding, which residents would be asked to vote on.
